why: Maya at her desk in a light office; her laptop screen fills most of the frame: a plain sign-in page, the password dots type in, the page turns to 'Welcome, Maya'
the frame splits: Maya's desk on the left, a second plain desk on the right with a person seen from behind; the same sign-in page on their screen, the same dots, the same 'Welcome, Maya'
both screens side by side showing the same welcome; an equals sign settles between them; the two people are different, the screens are identical
Maya's screen moves past the password to 'Enter the code'; her phone on the desk lights with six digits; she types them and the welcome returns

split again: the thief's screen accepts the password, then stops on 'Enter the code' with an empty box and a blinking cursor; across the split, Maya's phone lights with a code she did not ask for and stays on her desk
close on Maya's desk: the password field, her phone, her fingertip on the phone; each lights and takes a short label as it is named
beside the thief's stopped screen, two plain bars: risk without MFA, full; risk with MFA, shrinking to a sliver; '99.22%' named last with who measured it in small type under it
Maya's screen, large: a message with a link; the link opens a page identical to her sign-in; the address bar above it, large, reads a look-alike address beside the real one
everything holds: Maya's finger over the key, the code typed into the look-alike page; the question sits in the frame in silence
split screen: as each character appears on Maya's look-alike page, the same character appears on the thief's real sign-in page a moment later; the code lands, the thief's screen says 'Welcome, Maya'
Maya's phone and her typed code side by side; the typed code lifts off her screen and drifts across the split to the thief's side
her phone large in the frame; a key settles inside it behind the glass; her thumb touches the screen and it unlocks
the real sign-in page sends a small question to the phone; the phone sends back an answer card stamped with the real address; the key stays inside the phone the whole time
the look-alike page with the address bar shown very large, the extra word marked; the phone checks it and stays silent; across the split, the thief's screen waits with nothing arriving
three plain bars rise one per phrase, labelled texted code, phone prompt, security keys; the third bar carries the words no one fell instead of a number
the bars stay; one line settles under them; the third bar keeps a thin outline to say it is not a wall
back at Maya's desk; her phone shows a sign-in prompt with Approve and Deny; a second and third prompt stack on top
Maya's thumb on Deny; the prompts fall away; across the split, the thief's screen reads denied
the three things from the story side by side: the password field, the typed code, the phone with its key; each shows its outcome as it is named
three short lines, each appearing as it is said
back to Maya at her desk, the opening sign-in, calm; the thief's desk across the split goes dark
